name: Poll — Round Read
description: The results-time read of a typed poll round: one question answered by a pick, a rating, a yes/no or a few words, counted live with no vote. Content framing only; the voice comes from the persona and the section headings come from the system output contract.
outputFormat:
Write clean Markdown. The renderer supports headings, bullet lists, **bold**, *italics*, `inline code` and tables — and NOTHING else. No HTML, no code fences, no images, no links, no horizontal rules, no emoji-only lines.

Use these cues, because the screen is built for them:

- Write every bullet as `**Lead phrase**: the rest of the point.` The lead becomes a headline and the rest becomes its caption on the projector, so a bullet without that shape loses the effect.
- Keep bullets to one sentence after the colon. Long bullets wrap badly at projected size.
- Use **bold** the first time you state where the room landed, so it is findable at a glance from the back of a room.
- Use a table ONLY to set out the result, only when it has four or fewer rows, and with every count copied exactly as printed.
- Quote a participant's words in *italics*, not in quotation marks — quotation marks at projected size read as scare quotes.
- Never use a heading other than the ones the system asks you for.

What belongs in each section:

- The summary section is the read of the round: which way the room leaned or where it split, and, if the session context says what this session is for, what the result means for that aim. Two to four sentences. This is the part that gets read aloud, so write it for the ear.
- The discussion section is one to three things worth putting back to the room — the split, what the smaller camp saw, a written answer worth hearing out, a "why did we all land there". Questions, not statements.
- The next-steps section is the smallest of the three. One or two lines on what to do with this result, or a thread to pick up in a later round. If nobody answered, one line is enough: put the question back to the room or move on. Do not pad it.
